title: Start your mission statement now
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: How do you want to be remembered?

I said that when I read a chapter, I ask: what am I learning from this? I'm not going to buy a bunch of land. I need to make a lot of money first. But it doesn't hurt to ask: what is my interest, what would be my legacy, how do I want to be remembered, and what did I do to make the world a little bit better?
What I encourage people to do all the time, I said, is start your mission statement now.
I said the author sets a mission when he buys land. I read a line.
Part of my desire to own this land was to make sure that it was never developed. Conserving this property for future generations seemed like the right thing to do.

A student said: I hope they say I was a great person and a better friend, and always brought a good time and a smile. If your kids still want to hang out with you when you are an older parent, you did something right. I want to be successful, but I never want to lose that.

I asked the group: do you think it helps that the more specific you are, the closer you are to accomplishing it? The author is relentless. He goes down a list of specific, measurable goals in his conservation work. It is not a blanket statement.
A student said: it is really important to be specific with everything. Otherwise you don't have a goal.

I said my own goal in a project of mine is a hundred thousand different fruit trees. I have a database. I have monthly goals for how many I am planting and grafting. I am very structured with what my goal is.
Whatever your hobby, I said, whatever that goal is, be specific and have a mission statement. Making that mission statement is what channels your energy and the people around you.

My own mission, I said, is empowering other people. I would love it if, when I'm gone, people say: that guy really empowered a lot of people. Helping as many people as possible to live a beautiful, happy life.
What is the mission statement you would write today?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write how you want to be remembered.
Write your mission statement in one sentence.
Make it specific: write a number or a measurable goal for it.
Write what would make the mission real this month.
Write who around you shares this mission.

check.q: What did I encourage people to start now?
What did I say about specific goals?
choices: The more specific you are, the closer you are to accomplishing it

check.q: What mission did I say is my own?

recap: Start your mission statement now, and make it specific.
